intended_object: A reduced word in a Coxeter system (W, S): a word s_{i_1}⋯s_{i_k} in the simple reflections whose length k equals the Coxeter length ℓ(w) of the element w it represents. The intended object comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The definition says ω is reduced when the length of its product, ℓ(π ω), equals the length of ω. Here `cs.length` is the word length of an element with respect to the simple reflections, that is, the minimum length of a word representing it. Any word representing w therefore has length at least ℓ(w). So the equation ℓ(π ω) = |ω| holds exactly when ω has minimal length among the words representing π ω, which is the textbook definition of a reduced word. The definition is stated for an arbitrary Coxeter system, which is the natural generality. Mathlib has no other definition of this notion.
